# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 38 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 38 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_038_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 8 — Abstain from Evil; Practice Good

**1** I said, "Sir, I ask you now to show me the powers of the evil spirits, so that by knowing their deeds I may keep away from them." **2** He replied, "Listen to the deeds from which you must abstain. Abstain from evil-speaking, from adultery, from drunkenness, from wicked pleasure, from unlawful eating, from pride and boasting, from lying and theft, and from all such things. **3** Do you think these are small evils for a servant of God? No — adultery is a great evil, and drunkenness is a great evil, and pride and boasting are great evils. These great evils God's servants must abstain from. **4** Hear now also the works you must practice: help the widow; visit the orphan and the poor; redeem the servants of God from their tribulation; be hospitable to strangers; resist no one; be humble and more submissive than anyone; honor the elderly; practice righteousness; watch over brotherly love; endure insults with patience; bear no grudge; encourage those who are sick in soul; do not cast away those who have stumbled in faith but restore and encourage them; rebuke sinners; do not oppress debtors and the poor — and all similar things. **5** Do you think these are small goods for those who practice them?" "Not at all," he said. "They are very great things." **6** I said, "Sir, I would like to know which of these evils I am entangled in, so that I may turn from them." "Listen," he replied. "I will tell you. Your business dealings and the many transactions you have undertaken — do not let these consume you; rather, leave business aside and cling to righteousness. **7** For if you do not give up your entanglement in these many business dealings, you will be unable to keep the Lord's commandments. And if you do not keep the Lord's commandments, you will not be saved."

---

*LOGOS note: The virtue list in v. 4 is one of the most comprehensive early Christian ethical catalogs. It is deliberately organized around the marginalized: widows, orphans, the poor, strangers, debtors — those most vulnerable in Roman society.*
